A new look on the web, in the desktop app and on the phone, built on GlimStone 3.5, with settings in tiles, a card for every job and a phone app that opens on an overview again.

## ✨ Added

- **The phone opens on a new Overview.** Tiles at the top count the open conflicts, the findings and the trash, and each one leads to its page. Below them are the running jobs with their direction, progress and the files at work, the next scheduled runs, the last run with what it changed, and how full each target is. If the app lacks file access, a notice above the tiles leads to the setting that grants it.
- **The phone has a bar along the bottom with Overview, Jobs, Conflicts, History and More.** More holds Anomalies, Trash, Targets and Settings. A narrow browser window gets a bar of its own with Jobs, Conflicts, History, Settings and More.
- **What's new.** After an update, green dots mark what changed, and a window opens by itself on the release notes. New, in the Version card on the Info tile, opens it again with the notes on one tab and the list of changes on the other, and one button marks everything as seen.
- **A welcome page and an Info tile.** A new install opens on a page that says what ArrowLoop found and lists three steps to the first sync, or restores the jobs from a backup file. The Info tile shows the versions of ArrowLoop, GlimStone and rclone, checks GitHub for a newer release and downloads a bug report without passwords or keys. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- **More places for notifications.** Beside Matrix, ArrowLoop sends email, posts to an Apprise API server, pings Healthchecks.io when a run starts and ends, and speaks plain JSON, Discord, Slack, Gotify or ntfy over a webhook. Every channel has a switch and a test that says why it failed, and you choose between failed runs only and every run. The phone offers the same channels.
- **A note for a run far outside the usual.** From a job's last fifty successful runs ArrowLoop learns how many files a run deletes and copies and how long it takes. Once it has ten runs to go on, a run far past that gets a note such as "Files deleted: 412, usually 0 to 6". The note holds nothing back, and Report unusual runs on Safety net turns it off.
- **The anomaly notes can be switched off, and every job can have its own brakes.** With the notes off, Anomalies leaves the sidebar and the phone while the brakes keep holding runs. A job's brakes are set in the Brakes card on its page.
- **The settings tiles can go in an order of your own.** Drag a tile with the mouse, hold it on a touch screen, or move it with Alt and an arrow key. Reset under Look puts the order back.

## 🎨 Design

- **ArrowLoop follows GlimStone 3.5 on the web, in the desktop app and on the phone.** Warnings are orange, text comes in five sizes, a pressed button gives way a little, and Design offers System beside Dark and Light. Pages use the whole width of the window, and a field or a dropdown stands beside its name as a switch does. On the phone every control dims under a finger.
- **Settings is a column of eight tiles:** General, Look, Sync, Safety net, Targets, Security, Apps and Info. In a narrow window or a phone's browser the tiles become a strip above the cards, which then get the whole width. A search opens with / or Ctrl+K and still finds settings by the names they had before.
- **The sidebar holds Jobs, Conflicts, Anomalies, Trash and History.** Targets is a tile under Settings and can go back in the sidebar with one switch. Every page has an address of its own, and an old address leads to where the page is now.
- **Every job is a card, and every job has a page.** The card shows both sides, when the job runs and a strip of its last fourteen runs, with Run, Pause and a More menu that holds everything else, so you rarely need to open a job first. A held run or a waiting conflict shows in orange, never as synced. The job's page has its runs, the files it touched, the preview, the check, the duplicate search and its brakes, each in a card.
- **Findings and conflicts are cards that say everything.** A finding says what happened and since when, and offers Run anyway, Take back, Acknowledge and Open job; Show more opens the figures and the files in place. A conflict names the file with its full path, says why the two sides differ and shows each side's size, time and which version is newer. Its answers say what they do, such as Keep both files.
- **A schedule reads as a sentence**, such as Daily at 03:00, on a button that opens its editor. The default schedule on Sync works the same way, and Cron still takes an expression typed by hand.
- **Smaller layout changes.** History keeps Filter and Search in its card, and runs open in a window. Every card is titled with a noun for what it holds. Empty the trash is the main button on Trash, and a menu with one action is that action's button.

## ⚡ Improved

- **A job shows the settings it takes from the defaults, with their values, locked.** Override gives the job a value of its own, starting from the current one, and Use the default hands it back. This replaces one switch that changed five settings at once and hid their values. Brakes work the same way, on the web and on the phone.
- **Exceptions list the jobs that differ from the defaults.** The card on the Sync tile shows each such job with its own values and Use the default, and Safety net has the same card for brakes. While every job follows the defaults, the card stays away.
- **Connect storage and clouds has a search.** It narrows the list as you type, by the name shown or by rclone's own name, and ignores accents. Every kind of storage rclone ships now has a name, a group and in most cases a logo, and every field has a plain name. The phone's picker has the same search.
- **Stored passwords, keys and tokens show as Saved with Change.** The field appears only while you change it, and saving without touching it keeps what is stored, on the web and on the phone.
- **Test connection answers on its own button**, green with Connected or red with Not connected and the reason. A connected target shows how full it is as a bar under its name.
- **A failed run says why in your language**, for example that the destination is too full, a drive is not plugged in or a sign-in was refused, with the figures written your way. Anything else shows the engine's own English.
- **The phone's settings and job editor are easier to read.** A Synchronisation card near the top of Settings shows the default direction and schedule, and This phone gathers file access, notifications, background activity and the lock. The job editor has three cards instead of one per setting, and a refused Save says why under the field.
- **Keyboard and motion.** Windows keep Tab inside, close on Escape and hand the focus back to the button that opened them, and job cards open from the keyboard. Animations follow the motion setting and stand still when the system asks for less motion. On the phone, menus and dropdowns stay on screen in right-to-left languages.
- **The password reset is easier to follow.** Forgot password? is a button at the foot of the login, the reset form appears once the code is in the log, and the new password is typed twice.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Two accounts on one server are two places.** A job between two Nextcloud users, or between two access keys on one S3 endpoint, looked like a job pointing at itself, and ArrowLoop refused to start. A job whose two sides really are the same place now stops on its own and says why, and the other jobs keep running.
- **A saved secret goes only to its own server.** A Matrix token or mail password is sent only to the server it was saved for; after you change the server, type it again. Send a test needs a password when the engine listens on the network.
- **Notifications leave passwords out.** Messages and Healthchecks.io pings drop the passwords in a connection string and the output of a failed command before or after a run, as the bug report does. The bug report says only whether a mail address, a mail server or a Matrix room is set.
- **A job with its own direction keeps its own mode.** Direction and mode now go together, so a job set to run right to left no longer mirrors just because mirror is the default. A mirror or move without a direction of its own stops and says it needs one.
- **A job set to run only when asked stays that way** when a default schedule is set. Before, the default ran it on the clock.
- **A watched folder that was deleted and made again, or a stick plugged back in under the same letter, is watched again** within a minute instead of only on the schedule.
- **A run you allowed is not an unusual run.** Run anyway and Take back no longer leave a note about the deletions you just allowed, and the job does not learn from that run.
- **Healthchecks.io hears nothing while a job's drive is unplugged**, where it used to get a failed run at every turn.
- **A missed schedule no longer makes the page ask for the findings over and over**, tens of thousands of times until the browser gave up.
- **Smaller fixes.** The Cron field keeps the spaces you type. The file log and the run list wrap long paths instead of cutting them. Two folders with the same name are told apart by their parent folders. The duplicate search names its sides correctly in German and several other languages.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text is in all 42 languages**, the failure reasons and the What's new list included.
